findings.summary: The closing sentence still says "TWO of these duplicate" three lines under a DUPLICATED list that now has THREE bullets, and IdempotencyWindow.java:43 in the same commit says "THREE of which DUPLICATE". This is the second half of round 2's major finding, unfixed.
findings.detail:
Round 2's major named two false statements in src/main: the DUPLICATED list omitted the fifth limit, AND the summary 'TWO of these duplicate' was wrong. The list was fixed -- Sequencer.java:125-136 now carries 'A pod absent from an intermediate checkpoint's pods map' -- and the summary at line 140 was not. The result is that this commit SHIPS the exact defect the task exists to end, at two src/main sites that disagree with each other: Sequencer.java:140 says TWO, IdempotencyWindow.java:43 says 'WITH THE LIMITS {@link Sequencer} ENUMERATES -- THREE of which DUPLICATE'. Verified by reading the tree, not the diff: the <ul> at Sequencer.java:113-137 contains exactly three <li> elements (a superseded incarnation, a bare v0 slot, a pod absent from an intermediate checkpoint's pods map).

FAILURE SCENARIO, and it is the one this row was opened for: a reader orienting on the contract reads the emphasised closing paragraph -- the one sentence that states the SHAPE of the guarantee -- and takes away that two of the enumerated cases duplicate. They then count the list, find three, and have to decide which of two src/main statements in the same class is stale; if they resolve it the other way (trusting the summary over the list) they conclude one of the three bullets is not really a duplication and may drop it. The row's own argument is that 'a number goes stale the moment another is found' -- and the number went stale inside the very commit that made that argument, between the time the fifth bullet was added and the time the summary was re-read.

The cheap fix is TWO -> THREE at line 140. The fix that matches the row's own stated principle is to delete the count from the summary entirely (the list is the enumeration; the summary need only say 'some of these duplicate, which is the direction I2 forbids') AND from IdempotencyWindow.java:43, which introduces a brand-new count into a SECOND src/main file in a commit whose headline claim is that IdempotencyWindow 'now states the property by reference rather than restating it'. A count is not a reference; it is a restatement with one number in it, and it is a sixth site to drift when M5.52 or M5.55 lands.

findings.summary: The M5.34 done cell says "two of the four duplicate" after enumerating five limits, three of them duplicating, four sentences earlier in the same cell.
findings.detail:
The done cell lists REFUSED: (1) the pointed delta does not carry the triple, (2) the pointer names a delta that is gone; and DUPLICATED: (3) a superseded incarnation, (4) the bare v0 slot, (5) a pod absent from an intermediate checkpoint's pods map. Five limits, three duplicating. The cell then closes with 'SO THE HEADLINE IS NOT "ANSWERED" AND NOT "ANSWERED OR REFUSED": two of the four duplicate' -- wrong on both numbers, and stale for the same reason as Sequencer.java:140: it was written when the fifth had not been added.

FAILURE SCENARIO: M5.52 and M5.55 are the rows that will close two of the three duplicating cases, and their authors read this cell to learn what M5.34 concluded. 'Two of the four' tells them one duplicating case is already someone else's; there are three, two of which are unpinned in either direction. This is the same class of defect that required M5.27 and M5.32 to exist as whole rows -- a false count in backlog prose that a later author reasons from -- reintroduced in the done cell of the row whose subject is that very failure.

findings.summary: The MEASURED repro for the fifth limit drops the two load-bearing details of the configuration -- K=1 and that leader 2's commits come from a DIFFERENT pod -- so reproducing it as written does not reproduce it.
findings.detail:
Lines 133-135 read: 'MEASURED by review: leader 1 commits podb/i1 flushSeq 0, leader 2 commits twice and writes its own checkpoint, leader 3 takes the retry -- TWO deltas carry the segment; with the middle leader committing nothing, one.' The recorded measurement (and M5.55's row, which has it right) says leader 2 runs at K=1 and commits two flushes from a DIFFERENT pod. Both matter: without K=1 the two commits do not trigger a checkpoint at all and the walk never stops at epoch 2; and if leader 2's commits come from podb itself, podb IS in the intermediate checkpoint's pods map with a higher watermark, so the flushSeq 0 retry is classified a replay and REFUSED by the pointer branch -- one delta, the opposite outcome, and by a different mechanism.

FAILURE SCENARIO: someone re-deriving this before writing M5.55's pin follows the javadoc, sees one delta, and concludes the fifth limit was measured wrong or has since been fixed. Recorded rather than pressed: M5.55 is cited in the next sentence and carries the full configuration, so the information is not lost, and review.md rule 11 says fixing a minor is usually wrong.
